title: Cerebral Blood Flow-Based Resting State Functional Connectivity of the Human Brain using Optical Diffuse Correlation Spectroscopy
protocol: Power up the FD-fNIRS and DCS system for at least 10 minutes.
Measure the distance between nasion and inion on the subject’s head.
Mark a point that is 10% of the distance from nasion to inion with an ink marker.
Place an EEG 10/20 cap so that the marked point is between Fp1 and Fp2.
Mark the points between Fp1 and F7 for left cortex, and between Fp2 and F8 for right cortex.
Position multi-mode fibers (MMF) on the newly marked points.
Connect each MMF to the 785 nm laser light source.
Place single-mode fibers 2.75 cm away from the multi-mode fiber.
Place two fibers on the DLFC at locations “DLFC,1” and “DLFC,2”.
Place one fiber on the IFC at location “IFC”.
Replicate fiber placement on each side of the cortex for a total of six single-mode fibers.
Place another single-mode fiber 1 cm below the multi-mode fiber at location “Ds” in both sides of the cortex.
Connect each single-mode fiber to individual single-photon counting machines.
Turn off any lights and turn on the FD-fNIRS system to prepare for calibration.
Warm light sources and detectors by powering up the system for at least 10 minutes.
Maintain optimal accuracy and stability by allowing the system to run for a minimum of 20 minutes and maximum of 1 hour.
Run GUI-based data acquisition software.
Press the “auto-bias” button with the sensor attached to a calibration phantom.
If the overvoltage warning flashes, lower the detector gain.
Disconnect one source fiber from the detector and verify that DC is less than 20 counts per measurement period.
Power down the system if DC exceeds 20 counts; remove excess room light and repeat steps.
Verify proper signal level from every source and detector (above 100 and below 1,500 counts).
Press the “Calibrate” button in the GUI to perform calibration using a known phantom.
Log the calibration data for system performance record.
Do not look directly at light sources and fiber outputs to avoid eye damage.
Warm up the DCS laser light sources and SPCM by switching them on and allowing them to run for at least 10 min.
Adjust the fiber position, angle, and data acquisition timing to obtain a signal of at least 5,000 counts/s and below 1,000,000 counts/s.
Verify sufficient photon count levels from each detector by checking the monitor display.
Check the y-intercept of the autocorrelation curve displayed on the monitor for optimal fiber contact.
Tighten the elastic band around the subject to prevent motion artifacts but ensure it does not cause discomfort.
Check the autocorrelation curves on the monitor to confirm they decay to 1 for longer correlation time (τ > 10 ms).
Instruct the subject to minimize movements during the 8-minute measurement period.
Turn off the lights and position the subject comfortably with eyes closed.
Place the FD-fNIRS system optical probe on the forehead adjacent to the DCS probe.
Press the “Acquire” button in the FD-fNIRS acquisition GUI to start baseline measurements.
Collect static optical properties, absorption parameters, and scattering parameters (μa, μ's) using FD-fNIRS data.
After completing FD-fNIRS measurements, press the “Run” button in the DCS data acquisition GUI.
Begin data acquisition on the optical DCS measurements for a total of 8 minutes with a maximum 2 seconds integration time.
Repeat the experiment within 1 hour of the initial experiment if necessary.
Extract optical absorption and scattering properties from FD-fNIRS data using the slope method.
Import auto-correlation raw data from each of the eight channels into data analysis software for DCS.
Calculate the normalized diffuse electric field temporal autocorrelation function (g1 [r,τ]) from g2 [r,τ] using the Siegert relation.
Fit the normalized electric field autocorrelation function to obtain β, a constant proportional to detected spatial modes.
Use the analytical solution for g1 to obtain αDB, a blood flow-related parameter.
Fit DCS data to the decay rate model to determine CBFi.
Fit the model using optical parameters obtained from FD-fNIRS.
Determine CBFi and β as main fitting parameters.
Discard DCS data if autocorrelation function is significantly lower than 1.5 (β < 0.5).
Discard DCS data if autocorrelation curve does not decay to 1 for longer correlation time (τ > 10 ms).
Detrend quantified results using a second-order polynomial fit.
Apply zero-phase second-order Butterworth filter with passband of 0.009–0.080 Hz.
Use linear regression to obtain residuals from each channel against short distance measurement.
Calculate Pearson’s correlation coefficient between each pair of channels.
Transform the correlation value into a z-value using Fisher Z transformation.
Perform t-test to obtain p-value.
Apply false discovery rate (FDR) for multiple comparisons correction.
